heuristics.title: The Master Cocci Rule
heuristics.rule: All medically significant cocci are **Gram-positive**, EXCEPT the **Neisseria** genus (*N. meningitidis*, *N. gonorrhoeae*) and *Moraxella catarrhalis*, which are **Gram-negative diplococci**.
heuristics.explanation: If an exam question mentions a coccus and it is not Neisseria or Moraxella, it is Gram-positive (Staphylococcus, Streptococcus, Enterococcus).

heuristics.title: The Master Bacilli Rule
heuristics.rule: Most medically significant bacilli (rods) are **Gram-negative** (Enterobacteriaceae, Pseudomonas, etc.), EXCEPT five major Gram-positive rod groups: **Bacillus**, **Clostridium**, **Corynebacterium**, **Listeria**, and **Mycobacterium**.
heuristics.explanation: Remember the mnemonic: 'Basically, Clostridium, Corynebacterium, Listeria, and Mycobacterium are Positive Rods'.

heuristics.title: The Endospore Genera Rule
heuristics.rule: Bacterial endospores are produced *ONLY* by two Gram-positive rod genera: **Bacillus** (aerobic) and **Clostridium** (obligate anaerobic).
heuristics.explanation: No Gram-negative bacteria and no cocci form endospores. Spores contain calcium dipicolinate and withstand boiling; sterilization requires steam autoclaving at 121°C for 15-20 min.

heuristics.title: The Anthrax Capsule Exception
heuristics.rule: Virtually all bacterial capsules are composed of **polysaccharides** (*S. pneumoniae*, *N. meningitidis*, *H. influenzae*, *Klebsiella*), EXCEPT **Bacillus anthracis**, whose capsule is uniquely composed of **poly-D-glutamic acid** (a polypeptide).
heuristics.explanation: Poly-D-glutamic acid is encoded on plasmid pXO2 and is non-immunogenic because host proteases cannot cleave D-amino acid peptide bonds.

heuristics.title: Bacteria Not Seen on Standard Gram Stain
heuristics.rule:
Remember the high-yield mnemonic **'These Microbes May Lack Real Color'**:
• **Treponema** (too thin for light microscopy → Darkfield microscopy or silver stain)
• **Mycobacterium** (mycolic acid lipid wall resists crystal violet → Acid-Fast / Ziehl-Neelsen stain)
• **Mycoplasma** (lacks peptidoglycan cell wall entirely → no Gram reaction; membrane contains sterols)
• **Legionella** (poor intracellular uptake of counterstain → silver stain or urine antigen test)
• **Rickettsia & Chlamydia** (obligate intracellular, very small → Giemsa stain or NAAT)
heuristics.explanation: These bacteria require specific diagnostic techniques because standard Gram staining yields false-negative or uninterpretable results.

heuristics.title: The Triple Sugar Iron (TSI) Diagnostic Code
heuristics.rule:
TSI agar contains 0.1% Glucose, 1.0% Lactose, 1.0% Sucrose, and phenol red indicator (Yellow = Acid [A], Red = Alkaline [K]):
• **A/A (Yellow slant / Yellow butt)**: Glucose + Lactose/Sucrose fermented (*E. coli*, *Klebsiella*)
• **K/A (Red slant / Yellow butt)**: Glucose only fermented (*Salmonella*, *Shigella*, *Proteus*)
• **K/K (Red slant / Red butt)**: Non-fermenter, oxidizer only (*Pseudomonas aeruginosa*)
• **Cracks / bubbles in agar**: Gas production (CO2/H2) (*E. coli*, *Proteus*)
• **Black precipitate**: H2S production from ferrous sulfate (*Salmonella*, *Proteus*).
heuristics.explanation: Glucose is present in 1/10th the concentration; once depleted at ~12h, bacteria on the aerobic slant oxidize peptones to amines (reverting slant to red/alkaline), while the anaerobic butt stays yellow/acidic.
